newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya says distributing oil wealth to the people.
newsitem.headline: Libya says distributing oil wealth to the people.

text.p: Libya on Thursday said it had started distributing oil wealth to 50,000 families, fulfilling partly a promise made by leader Muammar Gaddafi to distribute half of oil revenue directly to the people.

The official Libyan news agency JANA, monitored in Tunis, said that the country's social security fund had opened banking accounts in foreign currencies for each of the 50,000 largest families registered with it and had credited each with $5,000.
In 1992, Gaddafi announced that each of Libya's some 600,000 families would receive between $7,000 to $10,000 in a direct distribution of half of Libyan oil revenues.
He said that the direct distribution was a dream of his revolution when he took power in 1969.
But there was no implementation of the pledge and Gaddafi said in a speech on September 2 that the payments would be limited to the poorest and largest families.
